issue_title: Empty table dumped when number of subtables > 1
issue_text:
When building a document programmatically, adding a single sub-table works fine, but adding a second sub-table under the same parent causes an empty parent table header to be dumped.

```python
import tomlkit

doc = tomlkit.document()

def add_table(parent, name):
    parent.add(name, tomlkit.table())
    return parent[name]

root = add_table(doc, 'root')
first = add_table(root, 'first')
print(tomlkit.dumps(doc))  # -> [root.first]   (correct)

second = add_table(root, 'second')
print(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
```

Output after adding the second table:
```
[root]
[root.first]

[root.second]
```

The empty `[root]` header should not be emitted; expected output is just `[root.first]` and `[root.second]` (a super table with only sub-tables and no direct key-value items should not render its own header).
test_command: python -c "import tomlkit; doc = tomlkit.document(); doc.add('root', tomlkit.table()); root = doc['root']; root.add('first', tomlkit.table()); root.add('second', tomlkit.table()); out = tomlkit.dumps(doc); assert '[root]\n' not in out, f'unexpected empty parent header: {out!r}'; assert '[root.first]' in out and '[root.second]' in out; print('OK')"
success_criteria: A super table containing only sub-tables (no direct key-value pairs) must not dump its own header; output contains only [root.first] and [root.second].
